evidence.supports: Confirms the June 24, 2026 Special Town Meeting vote approving a temporary BESS moratorium through Sept. 30, 2026, its purpose, and that it awaits Attorney General approval.
evidence.quote: In Chesterfield, voters at June 24's special Town Meeting approved a temporary moratorium on construction of battery energy storage systems, or BESS, through Sept. 30, 2026. The moratorium now awaits approval from the attorney general's office.

evidence.supports: Confirms the Planning Board finalized a permanent BESS zoning bylaw on 2026-09-15 ahead of a Sept. 30, 2026 Special Town Meeting vote, timed to precede the moratorium's Sept. 30 end date and the state's Oct. 1 fast-track solar rules.
evidence.quote: On Sep. 30, a special Town Meeting will be held in Town Hall... If the bylaw passes during the meeting, it will be forwarded to the state attorney general's office for a stamp of approval.

decisions.notes: The underlying June 24, 2026 Special Town Meeting vote for a temporary BESS moratorium through Sept. 30, 2026 is well documented and is genuinely a temporary pause, not a zoning change -- criteria (a)/(b)/(c) are satisfied. However, I searched further and found that the Massachusetts AG's office has an extensive, well-documented pattern in 2026 of disapproving almost identical local temporary BESS/solar moratorium bylaws in this same region under G.L. c.40 Sec.32 review (Worthington, Blandford, Northfield, Wendell all rejected/expired this year -- see gazettenet.com/2026/06/22/ag-rejects-solar-moratoriums-in-worthington/ and foleyhoag.com's March 2026 'AGO Rejects Yet Another Municipal Solar and Battery Storage Moratorium' post). No source confirms whether the AG approved or disapproved Chesterfield's June 24 moratorium specifically; the only evidence (Gazette, 7/7/2026) says it merely 'awaits approval.' A third-party BESS-moratorium tracker (carina.energy, as of August 2026) does not list Chesterfield among Massachusetts' active restrictions, though that tracker is visibly incomplete (it also omits several other confirmed MA rows in this inventory). Because the town was still racing to finish a *permanent* bylaw ahead of the moratorium's Sept. 30 end date (per the Sept. 16 Gazette article), the town itself appears to be treating the moratorium as currently operative. I could not confirm AG action either way within the search budget; leaving the row as 'active' is the better-supported call, but the coordinator should treat this as flagged for a possible AG-disapproval correction if evidence surfaces.

evidence.supports: Confirms the unanimous roll-call vote adopting the one-year moratorium, its 180-day extension mechanism, and that the Planning Board will study zoning impacts during the pause.
evidence.quote: City Council voted unanimously on Wednesday to adopt a one-year moratorium on data centers... if the Planning Board is unable to put forth recommendations in that time frame, City Council can extend the moratorium by 180 days

evidence.supports: Confirms the Planning Board (4-1) and Economic Development Committee (4-0) recommendations preceding the vote, the councilor who proposed it, and the trigger of Gov. Healey's Sept. 8, 2026 executive order.
evidence.quote: the Greenfield Economic Development Committee voted to recommend the City Council pass a one-year moratorium on data center construction... proposed by Precinct 7 Councilor Sarah Bolduc

decisions.notes: Verified against the Greenfield Recorder's Sept. 17, 2026 report of the unanimous Sept. 16 roll-call vote, one-year term, 180-day extension mechanism, and the Sept. 9 preceding-committee-vote article. Consistent, well-corroborated, no duplicate found.

evidence.supports: Confirms the Sept. 14, 2026 public hearing, that the Council postponed a decision pending the Planning Board's recommendation, and scheduled a further hearing for Sept. 28, 2026; names the petitioner (Council President Claire Freda) and the proposed end date (July 31, 2027).
evidence.quote: Council President Claire Freda submitted the petition, which would establish a moratorium beginning upon adoption and continuing through July 31, 2027... Later in the meeting, the council unanimously granted further time on the data center moratorium petition and scheduled another hearing on Sept. 28

evidence.supports: Confirms the two petitions (data centers and battery storage), the July 2026 unanimous Council vote to hold the required public hearing, that no data center or battery storage project currently exists or is proposed in Leominster, and that Mayor Mazzarella's approval would also be required.
evidence.quote: The petitions, filed by Council President Claire M. Freda, would pause data centers and battery storage facilities construction until July 31, 2027... Before the moratorium can go into effect, the petition would need to be approved by Leominster Mayor Dean J. Mazzarella.

decisions.notes: Verified: as of the Sept. 22, 2026 hearing, the Council had granted more time and scheduled a further hearing/vote for Sept. 28, 2026 (five days after this research date); no adoption had occurred. 'pending' is correct.
